nodes.summary: Let $m, j, i, r$ be natural numbers with $j \ge 1$ and $r < m$, and let $F_j$ be the Fibonacci $j$-numbers: $F_j(0) = 0$, $F_j(n) = 1$ for $1 \le n \le j$, and $F_j(n) = F_j(n-1) + F_j(n-j-1)$ for $n > j$. Then the number of permutations $\pi$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, im + r - 1\}$ such that $\pi(x) - x \in \{-m, 0, jm\}$ for every $x$ equals $F_j(i+1)^{m-r} \, F_j(i+2)^r$.
nodes.title: Counting strongly restricted permutations with displacements $-m$, $0$, $jm$

nodes.summary: Let $m, j, i, r, k$ be natural numbers with $j \ge 1$ and $r < m$, and let $f_n(x)$ be the $(1, j+1)$-bonacci polynomials with natural-number coefficients: $f_0(x) = 1$, and $f_{n+1}(x) = f_n(x) + x f_{n-j}(x)$ if $n \ge j$, $f_{n+1}(x) = f_n(x)$ if $n < j$. A fence $(s, g)$, with $s$ and $g$ natural numbers, has teeth in slots $s$ and $s + 1 + 2g$. nodes.summary: For every natural number $q$, the set $\{1, 2, \dots, q\}$ is well based.
nodes.title: The set $\{1, \dots, q\}$ is well based

nodes.summary: Let $l$ be a natural number and $\omega$ a binary word of length $l$, read as a natural number $\omega < 2^l$. Then the set $Q$ of those $j \in \{1, \dots, l-1\}$ for which the leftmost $l - j$ bits of $\omega$ differ from its rightmost $l - j$ bits, that is $\lfloor \omega / 2^j \rfloor \ne \omega \bmod 2^{l-j}$, is well based.
nodes.title: Subword shift sets are well based

nodes.summary: A finite set $Q$ of natural numbers is well based (Kitaev; Valyuzhenich) if for every $x \in Q$ and every natural number $a$ with $0 < a < x$, at least one of $a$ and $x - a$ lies in $Q$.

nodes.summary: Fix a natural number $s$ and put $t = s + 1$. The $(1,t)$-bonacci polynomials $f^{(t)}_n(x)$, $n \ge 0$, are the polynomials with natural-number coefficients defined by $f^{(t)}_0(x) = 1$ and, for every $n \ge 0$, $f^{(t)}_{n+1}(x) = f^{(t)}_n(x) + x \, f^{(t)}_{n-s}(x)$ if $s \le n$ and $f^{(t)}_{n+1}(x) = f^{(t)}_n(x)$ if $n < s$.
nodes.title: The $(1,t)$-bonacci polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $p$, $q$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $p < q < 2p$, let $Q = \{1, \dots, q\} \setminus \{p\}$, and let $S^Q_n$ be the number of subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ in which no two elements differ by an element of $Q$. Then $S^Q_n$ is the number of compositions of $n + q$ in which every part is either $1$ or of the form $q + 1 + jp$ for some integer $j \ge 0$.

nodes.summary: For a finite set $Q$ of natural numbers and $n \ge 0$, $S^Q_n$ is the number of subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ in which no two distinct elements differ by an element of $Q$. That is, $S^Q_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} S^Q_{n,k}$, where $S^Q_{n,k}$ is the number of such subsets with $k$ elements.
nodes.title: Number of subsets avoiding a set of differences

nodes.summary: For a finite set $Q$ of natural numbers and $n, k \ge 0$, the restricted combinations are the $k$-element subsets $s$ of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ such that $b - a \notin Q$ for all $a, b \in s$ with $a < b$. Since only distinct elements are compared, whether $0 \in Q$ makes no difference.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $\omega$ and $l$, the shift set of $\omega$ with length $l$ is the set of $j \in \{1, \dots, l - 1\}$ with $\lfloor \omega / 2^j \rfloor \ne \omega \bmod 2^{l-j}$. When $\omega < 2^l$ is read as a binary word of length $l$, this says that the leftmost $l - j$ bits of $\omega$ differ from its rightmost $l - j$ bits.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
